question: Can you calculate the 5-day symmetric moving average of predicted toy sales for December 5 to 8, 2018, using daily sales data from January 1, 2017, to August 29, 2018, with a simple linear regression model? Finally provide the sum of those four 5-day moving averages?
sql:
WITH regression_params AS (
    SELECT 
        0.5639098646455303::DOUBLE as slope,
        649.648518375471::DOUBLE as intercept
),
target_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE '2018-12-05' as target_date,
        (DATE '2018-12-05') - (DATE '2017-01-01') as day_diff
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        DATE '2018-12-06' as target_date,
        (DATE '2018-12-06') - (DATE '2017-01-01') as day_diff
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        DATE '2018-12-07' as target_date,
        (DATE '2018-12-07') - (DATE '2017-01-01') as day_diff
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        DATE '2018-12-08' as target_date,
        (DATE '2018-12-08') - (DATE '2017-01-01') as day_diff
),
predictions AS (
    SELECT 
        t.target_date,
        CAST(t.day_diff AS INTEGER) as day_num,
        r.slope * CAST(t.day_diff AS INTEGER) + r.intercept as predicted_sales
    FROM target_dates t
    CROSS JOIN regression_params r
),
moving_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        p.target_date,
        (r.slope * (CAST(p.day_num AS INTEGER) - 2) + r.intercept + 
         r.slope * (CAST(p.day_num AS INTEGER) - 1) + r.intercept + 
         p.predicted_sales + 
         r.slope * (CAST(p.day_num AS INTEGER) + 1) + r.intercept + 
         r.slope * (CAST(p.day_num AS INTEGER) + 2) + r.intercept) / 5.0 as moving_average_5day
    FROM predictions p
    CROSS JOIN regression_params r
)
SELECT 
    SUM(moving_average_5day) as total_sum_of_5day_moving_averages
FROM moving_averages
